question: What do you call the process of erosion due to the action of snow?
solution:
The correct answer is "**Nivation**".

__
 
• Hollows form under the emerging glacier as a result of the freeze-thaw cycle and mass wasting is known as **Nivation**.
 
• Nivаtiоn is the set оf geоmоrрhiс рrосesses аssосiаted with snоw раtсhes.
 
• The рrimаry рrосesses аre mаss wаsting аnd the freeze аnd thаw сyсle,in whiсh fаllen snоw gets соmрасted intо firn оr névé.
 
• Nivation now encompasses a number of related subprocesses that relate to snow patches that may be stationary or semi-permanent.
 
• These sub-processes include weathering, meltwater flow from beneath the snow patch, erosion (if any), and the start of erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bio-erosion describes the breakdown of hard ocean substrates – and less often terrestrial substrates – by living organisms.​
 
• 
 
Sedimentation is the deposition of sediments. It takes place when particles in suspension settle out of the fluid in which they are entrained and come to rest against a barrier.

 
 
• 
 
This material is usually **soil** and **rock**. Just as rivers carry along all sorts of debris and silt that eventually builds up to form deltas, glaciers transport all sorts of dirt and boulders that build up to form moraines.

 
 
• 
 
A moraine is material left behind by a moving glacier.
